plan.reason: Redis is a stateful, single-replica dependency on the cart and checkout paths. A pod failure directly tests whether the persistent volume preserves cart data and whether dependent services fail safely. The integrity criterion is required because silent cart loss is a possible customer-impacting failure.

prediction.summary: Cart operations and cart-dependent checkout requests are expected to fail during the outage. Stored cart data should remain intact after Redis recovery because a persistent volume is configured.

plan.reason: Cartservice is a single replica and is directly shared by frontend and checkoutservice. This tests whether the application exposes a customer-visible outage rather than merely observing that the target becomes unavailable.

prediction.summary: Cart access and checkout requests that use carts are expected to produce elevated errors while the cartservice is unavailable.

plan.reason: The frontend is the sole entrypoint and has one replica. A one-time kill tests both immediate customer availability and recovery after recreation, without relying on target health as a success criterion.

prediction.summary: Users are expected to see elevated request failures while the sole frontend pod is being recreated, potentially preventing site access and checkout initiation.

plan.reason: Network loss is unavailable in the current fault set, so moderate dependency latency is used to distinguish catalog timeout/latency propagation from a pure catalog pod outage. With two catalog replicas, customer impact will show whether redundancy actually prevents checkout degradation.

prediction.summary: Product browsing and product-dependent checkout flows are expected to become substantially slower and may generate errors if callers lack adequate timeout, retry, or fallback handling.

replan_note: No prior experiments exist, so ranking follows customer-impact risk: the stateful cart datastore and cartservice are tested first, followed by the sole entrypoint. V7 is included as a competing explanation test for dependency degradation; network_loss was unavailable, so network_delay is the closest permitted fault. No experiment uses unhealthy_count for the directly faulted target.
